documents.title: Persistent atrial fibrillation in older adults: Comparison of seven models and development of a gradient boosting machine classifier in a single-center observational study.
documents.abstract: This study aimed to investigate clinical correlates of persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) in older adults, compare seven classification models, and interpret the selected gradient boosting machine (GBM) classifier. This single-center observational study included 572 adults reported to be aged ≥ 60 years who received care between June 2021 and June 2023, comprising 385 participants classified as having persistent AF and 187 comparators. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) were used for candidate-variable assessment and f

documents.title: Machine-learning-assisted multi-omics profiling identifies CALB1 as a subtype-associated regulator of PI3K/AKT signaling and malignant progression in non-small cell lung cancer.
documents.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is molecularly heterogeneous, and computationally nominated biomarkers often lack sufficient functional validation. CALB1 is a calcium-binding protein, but its clinical relevance, cellular source, and signaling role in NSCLC remain unclear. This study aimed to identify subtype-associated regulators in NSCLC through a machine-learning-assisted multi-omics framework and to characterize the functional and signaling relevance of CALB1 in malignant progression.

documents.title: A survival-informed CD8+ T cell-associated gene signature and its prognostic relevance in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
documents.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by marked clinical and immunological heterogeneity, and conventional clinicopathological variables do not fully capture patient survival risk. CD8+ T cells play a central role in antitumor immunity, yet their functional states can encompass both effective cytotoxic responses and dysfunctional immune programs. This study aimed to derive a survival-informed CD8+ T cell-associated gene signature and evaluate its prognostic associations, cellular expression, and relationship to immune dysfunction.

documents.title: Development and validation of a phase-stable computed tomography radiomics model for brain metastasis risk stratification in non-small cell lung cancer.
documents.abstract: Brain metastasis (BM) is a frequent complication of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but individualized risk stratification remains limited. We evaluated whether computed tomography (CT) radiomic features reproducible across non-enhanced and contrast-enhanced phases could improve BM risk prediction and whether integration with clinical biomarkers and semantic CT findings provided additional value.

documents.title: From risk factors to individualized prediction: development and internal validation of a machine learning model for early identification of postoperative pneumonia after lung cancer surgery.
documents.abstract: Postoperative pneumonia (POP) remains one of the most common infectious complications following lung cancer surgery and is associated with substantial morbidity. Although several risk factors for POP have been identified, clinically applicable approaches for early individualized risk stratification remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate machine learning models for early prediction of POP using routinely available perioperative variables.

documents.title: Building from the ground up: augmentation strategies to improve protein language model performance on protein sets.
documents.abstract: An important underlying requirement for deep learning models is the availability of large datasets, however, in sciences such as chemistry and biology, generating experimental data of sufficient size represents a significant bottleneck. In this work, we probed the extent and nature of limited input data, characterize how several protein language models (pLMs) learned on suboptimal datasets, and investigated augmentation approaches to improve predictive model performance. documents.title: AI-based prognosis and chemotherapy benefit in node-positive, HR+ breast cancer: a blinded external validation on SWOG-8814 trial.
documents.abstract: The benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy varies among patients with postmenopausal, node-positive, hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. Genomic assays identify patients likely to benefit from chemotherapy but are expensive and tissue consuming. AI-enabled biomarkers may provide scalable alternatives. We performed a blinded external evaluation of Ataraxis Breast CTX, a causal multi-modal AI model that integrates H&E images with clinical variables, in the phase III SWOG-8814 trial.

documents.title: Functional architecture of rare protein coding variation across 786,871 exomes.
documents.abstract: Protein coding variants span the gamut of structural and functional effects on proteins, and they have similarly heterogeneous effects on traits. Their functional effects can be predicted and categorized, particularly using machine learning models, and integrating these predictors benefits gene discovery. However, it remains unclear how well known structural features and predicted functional scores explain the heterogeneous effects of protein coding variants on human complex traits. documents.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

documents.title: Predicting cell-state-specific gene regulation from DNA across species.
documents.abstract: DNA encodes the cell's phenotype, but the same DNA sequence is interpreted differently in every cell type, developmental stage, and activity state. Existing deep-learning models solve only half of this puzzle: sequence-to-function models read DNA but treat cell state as a fixed label, while single-cell foundation models represent cell state but not sequence. We developed Bolero, a sequence-to-function model whose parameters condition on atlas-scale cell-state embeddings and additional biological variables to predict cell-state-specific chromatin accessibility and transcript abundance from DNA.

documents.title: De novo Design of a Vanadium Haloperoxidase.
documents.abstract: Organohalogens are an essential class of compounds for both synthetic chemistry and natural systems, yet the design of halogenases to catalyze carbon-halogen (C-X) bond formation has remained elusive. Vanadium-dependent haloperoxidases (V-HPOs) are attractive targets for such an effort, but they pose an unusual design problem: the vanadate (VO 4 3- ) cofactor is an anionic oxometalate that must be held by a precisely arranged network of hydrogen-bonding and electrostatic interactions rather than by the strong coordinate-covalent bonds through which proteins bind cationic transition metals. documents.title: Distance-AF Multimer: A Multi-Step Approach for Protein Complex Structure Modeling with User-Defined Distance Constraints.
documents.abstract: The three-dimensional structure of proteins provides essential insight into the molecular mechanisms underlying their function. Many biological activities are mediated through protein interactions, making accurate structural determination of protein complexes important. Despite significant advances in computational protein structure prediction, there are still many cases where protein complexes are not correctly assembled. documents.title: Multimodal Integration Identifies C16orf74 as an EMT Regulator With Prognostic Relevance in HNSCC.
documents.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is an aggressive malignancy characterized by marked intratumoral heterogeneity and poor clinical outcomes. Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) promotes metastasis, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. However, the key molecular determinants underlying EMT-associated malignant states remain incompletely defined, and their translation into clinically accessible tools is challenging. In this study, we performed an integrative multiomics analysis to dissect malignant epithelial heterogeneity in HNSCC. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) i

documents.title: Estimating rates of SARS-CoV-2 lineage spread using graph spectra from genetic sequence data.
documents.abstract: The modern enormous scale of viral genomic data, as exemplified by SARS-CoV-2, presents unique opportunities for epidemic inference and real-time monitoring. A key challenge is to wade through the extremely large stream of sequence data in order to identify small subsets of sequences that may represent rapid population growth of newly emerged lineages. To address this challenge, we developed a new approach that combines techniques in graph theory and machine learning. We represent distances between small subsets of sequences as graph Laplacians and identify from them features of rapid populati

documents.title: EZpred: Improving Deep Learning-Based Enzyme Function Prediction Using Unlabeled Sequence Homologs.
documents.abstract: Features extracted from sequence homologs significantly enhance the accuracy of deep learning-based protein structure prediction. Indeed, homolog-aware models such as AlphaFold generally produce more accurate protein structures compared to single sequence-based methods like ESMfold. In contrast, features from sequence homologs are seldom employed for deep learning-based prediction of the biological functions of a protein, such as Gene Ontology terms or Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers. Although a small number of models also incorporate function labels from sequence homologs, they cannot utilize

documents.title: Preoperative discrimination of malignant and benign ovarian masses using cfDNA fragmentomics and serum biomarkers.
documents.abstract: Preoperative discrimination of ovarian cancer from benign masses poses significant challenges, particularly in cases where serum biomarkers yield negative or nonspecific results. This multicenter observational diagnostic modeling study analyzed plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) from 743 participants across training, internal test, external test, and two exploratory cohorts using low-pass whole-genome sequencing. Four fragmentomic feature classes-fragment size patterns, nucleosome footprint-related features, copy-number variations, and repeat element patterns-were incorporated into a stacked machine

documents.title: Bacterial protein function prediction via multimodal deep learning.
documents.abstract: Bacterial proteins are specialized with extensive functional diversity for survival in diverse and stressful environments. A significant portion of these proteins remains functionally uncharacterized, limiting our understanding of bacterial survival mechanisms. Hence, we develop Deep Expression STructure (DeepEST), a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts protein function in bacteria by assigning Gene Ontology (GO) terms. DeepEST comprises two modules: a multi-layer perceptron that uses gene expression and gene location, and a protein structure-based module that uses predicted struct

documents.title: Explainable AI identifies recombination and chromatin environment as key predictors of subgenome evolution in maize and Brassica.
documents.abstract: Polyploidy, or whole genome duplication, reshapes genomes through biased gene loss and regulatory rewiring, yet the drivers of biased fractionation among subgenomes remain unclear. Using maize and Brassica rapa as model allopolyploids, we compiled 60 genomic and epigenomic features in maize and 45 in B. rapa and constructed supervised machine learning models to classify genes by subgenome identity. In both species, eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) approaches identified recombination rate as the most influential and highly interconnected feature despite nonsignificant mean differences

documents.title: Development and Validation of Machine Learning Models Incorporating TGFBIp Expression for Prognosis Prediction in Epithelial Ovarian Cancer.
documents.abstract: Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) exhibits substantial heterogeneity in clinical outcomes, highlighting the need for diverse prognostic tools. Transforming growth factor-β-induced protein (TGFBIp) has been implicated in ovarian cancer progression, but its incremental prognostic value within machine learning frameworks remains unexplored.

documents.title: Metabolic Profiling Combined With Machine Learning for Assessing Clonal Hematopoiesis Status in Chronic Immune Thrombocytopenia: An Exploratory Analysis.
documents.abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) has emerged as a potential contributor to the pathogenesis of immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), yet the clinical and metabolic features of ITP patients harboring CH-associated mutations remain poorly characterized. We retrospectively analyzed a genomic discovery cohort of 1817 patients with chronic ITP, identifying CH in 196 individuals (10.8%), with DNMT3A as the most frequently mutated gene. In a metabolomic profiling cohort of 539 patients (492 ITP-non-CH, 47 ITP-CH), we characterized plasma metabolic signatures using untargeted LC-MS/MS and systematically evaluated t

documents.title: A machine learning-based predictive tool for complete renal response in lupus nephritis leverages the 3-month treatment milestone.
documents.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) remains a major determinant of poor prognosis in systemic lupus erythematosus, yet reliable tools for early identification of unfavorable renal outcomes are lacking. This study aimed to identify early prognostic factors for complete renal response (CRR) at 12 months in active LN and to develop interpretable machine learning (ML) models for early prediction of treatment response. In this prospective cohort of 400 active LN patients followed for 12 months, the primary outcome was 12-month CRR. Candidate predictors were assessed at baseline and 3-month follow-up. Four ML mode

documents.title: Predicting the alternative conformation of a known protein structure based on the distogram of AlphaFold2.
documents.abstract: AlphaFold2 (AF2) has become one of the most established and leading tools for predicting protein structures, although it often favors a single conformation. While it has been shown that sampling different conformations is possible by manipulating the multiple sequence alignment (MSA), the potential for multi-state information within a standard AF2 prediction remains underexplored. In this work, we demonstrate that even with a deep MSA, AF2 predictions encode structural heterogeneity. Specifically, we observe that the predicted residue-residue distance distributions often exhibit multiple proba

documents.title: Development of a Machine-Learning Model for Strongyloidiasis Risk Stratification in Migrant Populations.
documents.abstract: Strongyloidiasis is a parasitic infection with the potential for fatal hyperinfection, underscoring the need for screening strategies. A machine-learning model was developed and externally validated to support strongyloidiasis risk stratification among migrants from endemic areas.
documents.journal: Research and reports in tropical medicine

documents.title: A lightweight multi-branch transformer architecture for Kazakh Sign Language recognition under signer-independent conditions.
documents.abstract: Sign Language Recognition (SLR) in low-resource sign languages is still limited due to the lack of annotated data, high variability of signers, and lack of benchmarks; Kazakh Sign Language (KzSL) is a representative example of such a low-resource language. The proposed research introduces a novel method for isolated KzSL recognition based on a purpose-collected dataset of RGB video streams of five signers, represented by 1662-dimensional per-frame pose, facial, and hand landmark vectors extracted using MediaPipe Holistic. The final dataset consists of 39,979 gesture samples across 187 output c

documents.title: SelCysML: a hybrid ML-BLAST pipeline for the automated identification and functional annotation of bacterial selenoproteins.
documents.abstract: Selenoproteins are characterized by the incorporation of selenocysteine (Sec) via UGA codon recoding, play vital roles in redox homeostasis and enzymatic catalysis. Despite this biological significance, their computational identification remains challenging, and recent assessments confirm that public databases suffer from widespread annotation errors, often misclassifying these proteins. Current predictive tools frequently operate as "black boxes" with limited interpretability or lack integrated functional validation layers, which contributes to high false-positive rates and persistent ambigui

documents.title: Dietary amino acid composition and elevated fasting glucose in children and adolescents from four Chinese provinces: a cross-sectional study combining regression and machine learning.
documents.abstract: Using an integrated analytical pipeline that combines regression and machine learning, with nonlinear dose-response modeling, this cross-sectional study sought to examine dietary amino acid composition in relation to elevated fasting glucose (EFG) in children and adolescents.

documents.title: A reproducible open-data framework for interpretable breast cancer diagnosis and cytopathology education.
documents.abstract: Quantitative nuclear morphology links cytopathological assessment with interpretable diagnostic modeling and provides a practical foundation for teaching medical artificial intelligence. This study evaluated a reproducible framework that connects nuclear feature interpretation, malignant-versus-benign classification, and evidence-based assessment of diagnostic decisions.

documents.title: Identifying potential targets in endothelial to mesenchymal transition-mediated atherosclerosis using bioinformatics and machine learning.
documents.abstract: Endothelial to mesenchymal transition (EndMT) is a key driver of atherosclerosis (AS). This study integrated multiple RNA transcriptomic and single-cell transcriptomic datasets to identify shared gene expression signatures between EndMT and AS.

documents.title: Development and temporal validation of an explainable machine learning model for predicting in-hospital diabetic foot ulcer in patients with type 2 diabetes using inflammatory-nutritional composite indices.
documents.abstract: This study aimed to develop and temporally validate explainable machine learning models for predicting in-hospital new-onset DFU in hospitalized patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) using routinely available admission variables and inflammatory-nutritional composite indices.

documents.title: A deep learning model for automated assessment of neonates at risk of impaired breast crawl: a proof-of-concept video-based study.
documents.abstract: Timely initiation of breastfeeding is critical for newborn health. The breast crawl, an instinctive sequence of behaviors, is fundamental to this process. However, newborns vary considerably in their ability to complete the crawl, and current assessment relies on subjective endpoint observation. This approach cannot provide an early, objective measure of crawl competency or support timely intervention for at-risk mother-infant dyads.
